# Identifiers

A DHIS2 object is named twice: by its UID, which is always present and never changes, and by
its code, which is optional and human-chosen. Every resource in this guide carries both, so
a consumer can reconcile against whichever one its own system holds.

## The two identifier slices

Each generated instance slices `identifier` on the identifier system into exactly two:

- `dhis2id` - always the DHIS2 UID, under `http://dhis2.org/fhir/id/<object-kind>`.
- `dhis2code` - the DHIS2 code, under `http://dhis2.org/fhir/id/<object-kind>-code`.
  DHIS2 codes are optional and may hold characters FHIR does not allow in a code, so this
  slot repeats the UID whenever the object has no usable code. That is what lets the slice be
  mandatory and consumers skip the absence check; `d2w fhir validate` reports every object
  taking the fall-back, which is how the codes get filled in upstream over time.

The same pair reaches terminology as concept properties rather than as identifiers. Concept
codes are DHIS2 option UIDs, so the other
identifier rides along on the concept:

- `http://dhis2.org/fhir/property/dhis2-id` - the DHIS2 UID of the concept's source object.
- `http://dhis2.org/fhir/property/dhis2-code` - its DHIS2 code, falling back to the UID.

identifier can look up what it means:
